name: OpenAI
description: Creator of the GPT-4.1 API family and the GPT-5 line (GPT-5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, and the current GPT-5.6 family of Sol, Terra, and Luna).

name: Anthropic
description: Creator of the Claude models, offered only as a hosted service through the Claude API and partner clouds.

name: Google DeepMind
description: The Google research team that builds the Gemini models, formed by combining Google Brain and DeepMind.

name: Meta
description: Creator of the Llama models, published as downloadable weights under Meta's own community licences.

name: SpaceXAI
description: The creator of the Grok models, served through a hosted API with no downloadable weights. Its own surfaces do not agree on one name: x.ai titles its news pages "SpaceXAI" and carries the footer "© 2026 SpaceXAI LLC", while the developer documentation on docs.x.ai describes the same models as "SpaceXAI’s frontier model" and the interface as "the xAI API". Both names are first-party and nothing checked on either site states a rename, so both are recorded and neither is asserted to have replaced the other.

name: Mistral AI
description: A French creator that publishes downloadable weights on its verified Hugging Face organization alongside a hosted API, and that uses more than one licence across the models it publishes. Its Hugging Face display name is written "Mistral AI_"; the trailing underscore is treated as a display artefact rather than part of the name.

name: DeepSeek
description: A Chinese creator that publishes open weights under the MIT licence. Both www.deepseek.com and api-docs.deepseek.com failed at the transport layer when checked on 2026-08-28, on two independent attempts each, so no page on the creator’s own domain could be read. The website and release page recorded here are its verified Hugging Face organization, which is the first-party surface that could be reached, and every DeepSeek fact in this dataset is read from there rather than from the creator’s own domain.

name: Alibaba Cloud
description: The creator of the Qwen model family. The Qwen team’s own Hugging Face organization states that Qwen "refers to the large language model family built by Alibaba Cloud", and this dataset records Alibaba Cloud as the creator on that basis. The team does not write the attribution identically everywhere: the QwenLM/Qwen3.8 repository credits "Qwen team, Alibaba Group", the parent company, while the Hugging Face profile credits Alibaba Cloud. That conflict is recorded rather than resolved. Qwen models are offered by clouds Alibaba Cloud does not operate, including Amazon SageMaker JumpStart; being served somewhere is never evidence of who built the model.

name: Microsoft
description: A company that occupies three roles this dataset keeps apart. It creates model families, through Microsoft AI, which builds the MAI line, and through Microsoft Research, which publishes the Fara line; those are the only Microsoft records treated as models. It ships Microsoft Copilot, which is a product and is recorded as one. It operates Microsoft Foundry, which is a serving platform and is recorded as one. A model appearing in Microsoft Foundry is a deployment fact and never evidence that Microsoft created it.

name: Amazon
description: The creator of the Amazon Nova model family, which AWS states is "built on AI technologies originally developed for Amazon’s internal applications". Amazon also operates Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, which serve models created by other organizations — Bedrock’s own page offers "hundreds of FMs from leading AI companies" — and this dataset records those as serving platforms, never as evidence of authorship. Amazon’s announcements are published by Amazon Web Services, whose wording alternates between naming Amazon and naming AWS as the announcing entity.

name: Cohere
description: The creator of the Command models, which its own model cards attribute to "Cohere Inc.". Cohere reaches customers through its hosted API, where it separates free "trial" keys from billed "production" usage, and publishes some models as downloadable weights as well. Cohere Labs is Cohere's research arm and the voice behind the separate Aya line; the clouds that resell Command models are serving platforms, not co-creators.

name: Allen Institute for AI
description: A Seattle-based nonprofit research institute whose OLMo project releases fully open language models, publishing weights, training data, and code.

name: Technology Innovation Institute
description: An Abu Dhabi government research institute whose AI unit develops the open-weight Falcon family of language models.

name: NVIDIA
description: A US technology company whose research teams publish the open-weight Nemotron model family. Its separate hardware and inference-platform roles are not recorded here as creator facts.

name: AI21 Labs
description: An Israeli AI company that builds the Jamba family of hybrid SSM-Transformer models, released as open weights and offered through its paid API.

name: Zhipu AI
description: A Chinese AI company, originating from Tsinghua University research, that develops the open-weight GLM model family and offers paid API access.

name: Moonshot AI
description: A Chinese AI company that develops the Kimi model family, released as open weights and served through its paid API.

name: EleutherAI
description: A non-profit research lab that states its focus as the interpretability, alignment, and ethics of artificial intelligence, and publishes its open models on Hugging Face. It develops the Pythia suite and the GPT-NeoX training library.

name: LG AI Research
description: The research organization that develops and releases the EXAONE family of instruction-tuned bilingual English and Korean language models, published under its own LGAI-EXAONE namespace.

name: Snowflake
description: The company whose Snowflake AI Research team pre-trained the Arctic dense-MoE hybrid language models from scratch and published the weights under Apache-2.0.

name: Upstage
description: The company that develops the Solar language models, built with a depth up-scaling method that extends a smaller model into a larger one.

name: IBM
description: The company behind the Granite family of open-source language models, which it describes as built for enterprise and research use and releases under the Apache 2.0 licence.

name: Baidu, Inc.
description: The company behind the ERNIE model line, whose 4.5 generation it publishes as a family of large-scale multimodal models under the Apache License 2.0.

name: Tencent
description: The company behind the Hunyuan model line, which spans text, image, video and 3D generation and is published under Tencent’s own community licence rather than an OSI-approved one.

name: ByteDance Seed
description: ByteDance’s Seed team, the research organization that develops and publishes the Seed model line. It is recorded as the creator of those models and is deliberately kept separate from ByteDance’s consumer assistant products, which this dataset does not record.

name: Stability AI Ltd.
description: The company behind the Stable Diffusion text-to-image models, published under its own community licence, which is free below a stated annual revenue threshold and requires a paid enterprise licence above it.

name: Databricks, Inc.
description: The data and AI platform company behind DBRX, a mixture-of-experts language model whose weights it published under its own open model licence while also serving it to its customers through APIs.

name: MiniMax
description: The AI company that develops the MiniMax-M1 hybrid-attention reasoning models, published as open weights under the Apache License 2.0 and sold as API access under its own name.

name: Apple Inc.
description: Recorded here only as the creator of OpenELM, a family of open efficient language models published with weights, training code and a licence that restricts them to scientific research. No page read for this record describes a paid model product or hosted model access from Apple.

name: Hugging Face
description: Recorded as a creator only for the models it makes itself, of which SmolLM3 is the one in this dataset. Hugging Face also operates the Hub that hosts most other creators’ model cards and weights, but hosting is where a source lives rather than who made a model: cards written by other creators are recorded under those creators, and the Hub’s own machine-readable records are the only sources attributed to Hugging Face as a platform.

name: 01.AI
description: The company behind the Yi series of open-source language models, which it states are trained from scratch and distributes, for the Yi-1.5 series, under the Apache 2.0 licence.

name: Sakana AI
description: A research-focused company that states its core focus is applying nature-inspired ideas such as evolution and collective intelligence to creating foundation models, and that released a set of Japanese-language foundation models produced by its Evolutionary Model Merge method.

name: Sarvam AI
description: The company behind Sarvam-M, a language model post-trained on Indian languages alongside English, which it publishes as part of what it describes as building towards a sovereign AI ecosystem in India.

name: NAVER Corp.
description: The Korean internet company behind the HyperCLOVA X generative AI line. Its English newsroom calls that line “NAVER’s generative AI” and the card for the model recorded here says the model “is a model developed by NAVER”, which is what this dataset records the creator on. The same announcement attributes the open-source SEED release to NAVER Cloud — “NAVER Cloud (CEO Kim Yuwon) announced the completion of three lightweight HyperCLOVA X SEED models” — and that is stated here rather than collapsed into NAVER or split off as a second creator. The relation between them is stated, by the model’s own licence agreement: “NAVER Corp., as the holder of the intellectual property of the Model, and its affiliate, NAVER Cloud Corp., as the exclusive business operator of HyperCLOVA X, enter into this Agreement with you.” Section 9.2 of the same document adds “NAVER Corp. owns the Model”. So the creator recorded here rests on a stated ownership relation rather than on the absence of one, and NAVER Cloud Corp. is not a second creator: the role that sentence gives it is operating the business, which this collection keeps separate from creating the model.

name: Aleph Alpha GmbH
description: The German AI company behind the Pharia model line. Its own blog announces "our new foundation model family that includes Pharia-1-LLM-7B-control and Pharia-1-LLM-7B-control-aligned", and the recorded release rests on that page. No paid model offering is stated on any page read for this record, so the organization type rests on the centrally-operated-creator fallback rather than an asserted sale.

name: Reka AI, Inc.
description: The AI company that builds the Reka Flash models. Its own news post states "we are excited to open source a few of our building blocks", naming Reka Flash 3.1, which is what the recorded release rests on. No paid model offering is asserted here from the pages read, so the organization type rests on the centrally-operated-creator fallback.

name: Nous Research
description: The maker of the Hermes model line, which its own site's structured metadata and footer both describe as "The AI accelerator company". Its releases page dates each release, and the recorded Hermes-4-14B release rests on that page. The company type is recorded rather than community: nothing read here states that contributors outside the entity's own appointment chain decide its releases, so the independent-contributor clause is not claimed, and the self-description as a company settles it.

name: Liquid AI, Inc.
description: The AI company behind the Liquid Foundation Models (LFM). Its own blog states "Today, we release LFM2", which is what the recorded release rests on. No paid model offering is asserted here from the pages read, so the organization type rests on the centrally-operated-creator fallback.

name: Xiaomi Corporation
description: The consumer-electronics and technology company whose MiMo reasoning models are published by its LLM-Core team under the XiaomiMiMo account. The MiMo repository states "we present MiMo-7B, a series of models trained from scratch and born for reasoning tasks", which the recorded release rests on. The organization type rests on the centrally-operated-creator fallback: no page read here states that Xiaomi sells model products or access under its own name.

name: AI Singapore
description: Singapore's national AI programme, which develops the SEA-LION family of Southeast-Asian language models. Its SEA-LION v3 model card records "Developed by: Products Pillar, AI Singapore" and "Funded by: National Research Foundation, Singapore". As a national research-funded programme whose institution controls its releases and which exists primarily for research, it is recorded as a research-lab rather than a company.
